title: Between-phonation RPDE variability fails a stable cross-cohort incremental Parkinson-classification test
abstract: We tested within-person RPDE variability beyond mean conventional and nonlinear voice measurements using public Little and Istanbul cohorts. Source records contained32 distinct subject codes despite31-person documentation; the target contained252 people. Target log loss changed2.821072 to2.793236, but source leave-one-code-out prediction worsened, the source-and-target-refit95% interval for the difference crossed zero [-0.409566,+0.193923], and a spline-baseline challenge reversed the increment. Both primary models transferred worse than a source-prevalence constant. The registered stable-improvement criterion failed. Domain shift, possible feature-extraction differences, unresolved source identifiers, small source size and confounding prevent a biomarker or clinical-utility claim. Two clean offline runs reproduced results exactly.
